newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM AGAINST POSSIBLE LYONNAISE, SUEZ MERGER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM AGAINST POSSIBLE LYONNAISE, SUEZ MERGER.

text.p: A possible merger between French Compagnie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux would hurt the interests of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA and the Belgian state, Belgian Economics Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo said in a statement on Wednesday.
Tractebel is a unit of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) , itself a unit of Suez.
Tractebel and Lyonnaise are both active in public utilities and waste management services.
"A merger, if it were to go ahead, would affect the strategy of SGB, and thus of Tractebel and the Tractebel units, notably operating in the energy sector in Belgium and abroad," Di Rupo said.

"The envisaged merger, even if it were only a partial merger, would seriously damage Belgian interests. Several of Tractebel's business activities are identical or close to those of Lyonnaise. Thus, Tractebel..could have a conflict of interest with its parent company, in Belgium as well as abroad," he added.
Di Rupo said he would study how to block the movement to other countries of decision centres of strategic industries.
Tractebel is mainly active in electricity production and gas distribution, which Di Rupo's ministry is responsible for regulating.
Lyonnaise is mainly active in water. Both groups are active in waste management.
In recent years, Tractebel has repeatedly run into political resistance from Flanders, Belgium's Dutch-speaking northern half, because it is French-owned.
Tractebel parent SGB, 63 percent owned by Suez, controls key sectors of the Belgian economy, such as banking, energy, insurance and several blue-chip industrial companies.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
